I don't think these car companies are in the wrong here, they're just being lazy(I'll explain).

Their endgame is most likely that they want to prevent people from modifying code in their vehicles because if something goes wrong they don't want to be legally responsible. I think that's fair. There should be legal protection for them if a modification in the code is what caused the issue.

What kind of legal protection should be implemented though? What if someone modifies the code in their vehicle but that isn't what caused the malfunction? This could get very tricky to prove and I'm sure would be a legal nightmare. No one wants to deal with that... Let's just make a law that says if you modify the software the car manufacturer is not at fault for ANY issues (unless it's proven to be hardware related and not caused by software at all).

Okay manufacturers are off the hook now. Should people be allowed to modify that code though? Manufacturers have to adhere to regulations and must test vigorously. Should someone be allowed to just make some codes changes and now drive on the road with other people? The answer is probably no.

So basically we need a law that says people can't modify code on their car, period. This is because manufacturers need legal protection when cars malfunction due to modified code AND for our safety so we don't have to drive around with other people who could potentially harm us.

Here's where the laziness comes in... Rather than write up some new law and try to lobby it and get it passed and waste time and money, they're just piggybacking on the DMCA to get the same desired results as stated above.

Personally I think there should be a separate law pertaining only to cars/vehicles because I don't like the existing DMCA. I should be allowed to modify software on things that I purchase UNLESS the thing in question weighs several tons and travels 60mph.

This is all speculations though, I have no idea what their actual motives are.
